newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Elec. picks suppliers in retail power pilot.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Elec. picks suppliers in retail power pilot.

text.p: Six electricity suppliers have been chosen for a one-year pilot program to provide retail power to four Massachusetts towns, part of the state's move toward a deregulated power market, officials said Thursday.
The program, set up by Massachusetts Electric, owned by New England Electric System, is set for a January 1, 1997, launch.

The six participants are; AllEnergy Co, a venture between New England Electric System and Eastern Enterprises ; Enova Energy of San Diego; Northeast Utilities (NU), NU affiliate Northfield Mountain Energy; a venture between Wheled Electric Power in Boston and Cynergy in Ill., and Working Assets Green Power of San Francisco.

Steven Rothstein, head of Environmental Futures, a private company that Massachusetts Electric hired to select the suppliers and the programs, said the pilot will allow up to 10,000 residential and small commercial customers to choose their electricity supplier.
Mass Electric already has a separate pilot program for industrial users.
"We think that, depending on which supplier the customer chooses and which program they use, there are potential savings of 10 to 15 percent," Rothstein said.

He added that with little publicity, his group had already received calls for more information on the pilot from more than 3,000 customers in the participating towns of Lynn, Lawrence, Northampton, and Worcester.

"Mass Electric knows that deregulation is coming. It's expected in early 1998...This is a year-long program. It starts in January. That will allow them to see how it will work on an experimental basis," Rothstein said.
Sorting out customer billing from a variety of power generators will be one of the main tests of the program.
Though customers will be able to chose their suppliers, Mass Electric will still manage the transmission and distribution of electricity on the local grid.
